subject: Dedicated runway: GPU family, TPS split & fallback plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated runway: GPU family, TPS split & fallback plan

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed asks so we can size a clean Dedicated POC and map to a longer-term Private/VPC path: 

Recap from call:
- Primary preference: Dedicated capacity to start for predictable performance and cost isolation; plan to migrate to Private VPC in Q4 after procurement.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline with periodic spikes; you estimated sustained 60 TPS with burst capacity to ~120 TPS for 10-15 minute windows.
- Token mix: median end-to-end tokens ~600 (prompt+completion) with a 95th percentile up to ~2,000 for long batch jobs.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 250ms for chat flows; batch/async can tolerate higher.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + KMS integration required for production.

Follow-ups we need from your side to finalize sizing: 
1) Confirm the 60 TPS sustained / 120 TPS peak numbers and typical burst duration (minutes).
2) Percent of requests that are short chat (<200 tokens) vs long generation (>1k tokens).
3) Any hard constraints on instance-level concurrency per tenant (e.g., must enforce per-customer concurrency caps).
4) If you plan to run multiple models in parallel, list models + expected traffic split (rough names are fine).

What we recommend for POC (high-level):
- Run a 2-week Dedicated trial with a small reserved pool + autoscaling bursts.
- Two candidate GPU families for the POC: H100-class for latency-sensitive + large-context models; A10/A30-class for cost-efficient throughput on smaller models.
- Configure prefix/KV caching for chat to reduce recompute on short flows; enable int4 quantization where model quality is acceptable.

I attached a short workbook that maps TPS/token mixes to a few pool options. If you can reply with the clarifications above, Ben and I will produce a recommended initial pool (exact GPU counts & estimated monthly units) and an ops/fallback ladder (what falls back to hosted API / smaller instances if capacity saturates).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Daniel Park <daniel@novuslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Li <tom@novuslabs.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated runway: GPU family, TPS split & fallback plan

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed numbers: our telemetry shows baseline ~55-65 TPS steady state; we see 10–20 minute bursts up to 110–130 TPS during peak campaigns. Bursts are roughly 12 minutes on average.
- Token mix: ~65% of calls are short chat flows (<200 tokens), ~30% medium (200–1,000 tokens), ~5% long (>1,000 tokens). There are nightly bulk jobs that can spike the long tail.
- Concurrency: we prefer soft per-tenant concurrency caps (e.g., 8 concurrent streams) rather than hard blocks — want to avoid noisy-neighbor issues.
- Models: initially one main Llama-variant ~13B for chat + a 65B for long-form summarization (fallback jobs). Expected split ~80% 13B, 20% 65B by request count, but the 65B consumes more tokens.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is a must for production; we also need KMS integration for key control prior to private deployment.

I've attached our security questionnaire and a one-pager on tenancy requirements. We're comfortable starting with Dedicated if the POC shows predictable latency and a clear migration plan to Private VPC. Next availability for a POC kickoff is the week of June 8.

—Daniel
Daniel Park | Head of Platform, Novus Labs
Daniel.Park@novuslabs.com | +1 (650) 555-0142

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated runway: GPU family, TPS split & fallback plan

Marissa / Neha — quick sizing + ops thoughts based on Daniel's clarifications: 

Assumptions pulled from their reply: sustained 60 TPS, peaks to 130 TPS for ~12min, token mix heavy on short chat (65%) but 65B model exists for heavier tasks. Avg tokens overall ~600, 95th up to ~2k.

Recommend two candidate POC configurations (tradeoff: latency vs cost):

Option A — Latency-first (recommended if 95p latency matters):
- GPU type: H100-class nodes (best single-GPU throughput for 65B workloads and lower per-request latency).
- Pool sizing: start with 3 H100s reserved + 1 H100 burst (total 4) — conservative estimate: ~25–40 effective chat TPS per H100 depending on batching and quantization; 3 reserved should cover baseline + small headroom; bursts handle campaign spikes.
- Concurrency: tune per-GPU concurrency to 8–12 live requests; enforce soft per-tenant cap of 8 as requested.
- Notes: enable KV/prefix caching for chat flows to cut token work on repeated turns; for 65B, expect lower TPS — route heavier jobs to dedicated smaller batch window or scheduled slots.

Option B — Cost-efficient (recommended if cost + volume matter):
- GPU type: A30/A10-class nodes (more cost-effective for 13B model); consider an A30-focused pool for the 13B chat workload.
- Pool sizing: ~8–10 A30s reserved to hit similar throughput against 13B (each A30 gives higher effective chat throughput on smaller models).
- Concurrency: higher per-GPU concurrency (12–20) with batching, but tail latency will be higher; use H100 pool as overflow for latency-sensitive requests.

Operational ladder / fallback plan:
1) Primary route to Dedicated pool (H100 primary, A30 overflow for 13B).
2) If Dedicated pool reaches saturation, automatically spill lower-priority jobs to Hosted API with quality-profiled model variant.
3) Implement rate-limits and tenant concurrency caps to protect baseline SLOs.

Quantization & model guidance:
- For 13B chat: int4 quantization is likely acceptable and gives a 2–3x throughput boost; A30 is solid here.
- For 65B: prefer H100s with FP16 or optimized int8 where we validate quality.

Next steps I can take:
- Produce a short cost/throughput table (GPU count, est TPS, monthly cost) using the workbook Marissa attached.
- Draft POC scope for a 2-week Dedicated test: metrics to measure (95p latency, successful requests/sec, cost per 1M tokens), and migration checkpoints for Private VPC.

I can have the spreadsheet updated and POC scope ready by Friday if we get Daniel's confirmation.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-05-29T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated runway: GPU family, TPS split & fallback plan

Daniel — perfect, thanks for the details. Proposed next steps so we can lock calendars: 

1) I'll share Ben's updated workbook + a short POC scope doc by Friday (includes two pool options, estimated GPU counts, and target success criteria).
2) Can you confirm the week of June 8 for a 30–45 minute kickoff? If June 8/9/10 work, I'll send a calendar invite and a brief agenda (kickoff, security checklist, success metrics, migration timeline to Private VPC).
3) We'll include KMS integration as a must-have for production signoff; Ben will note any gaps in the questionnaire you attached.

If you're OK, we'll propose starting the POC with Option B (A30 pool for 13B chat) + a small H100 buffer for the 65B jobs, then iterate after a week if latency isn't hitting the 95p target. That approach keeps initial cost down while proving the migration path to Private.

Let me know which kickoff date works and we'll get the paperwork in motion.

Thanks — Marissa
